summary: Iteration 42: WhatsApp FocusChat-style chat layout (Phase 1) tested end-to-end. Backend: 15/15 pytest tests pass — /attendants auto-creates Isabella (idempotent), /conversations returns {buckets:{automatico,aguardando,fora_de_hora,manual,grupo}, items[]} with counts matching items length, @g.us → bucket='grupo', PUT /assign with human → bucket='manual' (also returns assignee_user_id/role), PUT /assign with ai → bucket='automatico', /finalize sets status='closed', /conversations/{phone}/messages returns ascending order, _maybe_auto_reply skips when assignee_role='human' (no auto_reply key in response, no outbound row created — verified via /conversations/{phone}/messages), 404 on assign to unknown user. Regressions pass: /qr, /status, /messages, /auto-reply GET, /voice/sessions/start, /aihub/agents/text-gen. Auto-reply left DISABLED at end of run. Frontend: WhatsApp REAL-connected (+5521965680949 'Patrocínio'). [data-testid=wa-chat-layout] + [data-testid=wa-buckets-sidebar] render. All 5 buckets present with counts {Automatico:10, Aguardando:0, Fora_de_hora:0, Manual:2, Grupo:2}. Clicking bucket → 10 conv items shown, clicking conv opens wa-chat-thread, wa-take-over-btn present and opens wa-assign-modal with 7 attendant pick buttons. ONE BUG FOUND: Isabella (IA) appears in the assignment modal — spec says she must be filtered out so an operator never accidentally assigns the bot to itself.

ui_bugs.issue: Isabella (IA) is listed as a pick option (wa-assign-pick-{isabella_id}). Per spec she must be filtered out — only human attendants should be assignable. The 'Devolver para IA' is supposed to be a separate action.

action_items: Frontend: Filter Isabella (IA) out of the AssignModal attendants list — either skip items where email==='isabella@ia.local' or where is_ai_agent===true. Add a separate 'Devolver para IA' button in the modal/thread that calls PUT /assign with {assignee_user_id:null, assignee_role:'ai'}.
critical_code_review_comments: [CARRY-OVER iter40/41] /api/whatsapp-baileys/inbound is now properly token-protected (verified — calls without X-WA-Token return 401). Good.
/conversations endpoint hardcodes DEMO_COMPANY_ID via user.company_id but other endpoints (e.g., inbound_webhook) still use DEMO_COMPANY_ID directly — same multi-tenancy gap noted in iter40/41.

_bucket_for_conversation uses 'fora_de_hora' calc with hour_brt — datetime.now(timezone.utc) - timedelta(hours=3) is hacky (assumes BRT=UTC-3 always, ignores DST. Brazil is currently UTC-3 year-round but worth a constant or pytz/zoneinfo).

GET /conversations does aggregate over aihub_wa_messages with $limit 200 BEFORE grouping by phone — if there are >200 message docs but they're concentrated on few phones, some convs may be missed. The $sort+$group+$limit order is good for performance but $limit should ideally be applied AFTER $group (move it after the $group stage). Minor edge case.
Frontend AssignModal bug (see frontend_issues): Isabella should be filtered out of the pick list.
seed_data_creation: Inserted ~4 unique-phone inbound messages per run via /inbound (TEST_iter42_* message_ids, phones 5521991[1-4]{xxxx}). Phones are randomized per run via uuid suffix so no cross-test pollution. wa_conversations docs created via /assign. Isabella user 'usr-isabella-co-demo' left in db as system fixture per request.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Run: pytest /app/backend/tests/test_iter42_whatsapp_chat.py -v. Tests are idempotent (uuid-suffixed phones). WhatsApp is REAL-paired (+5521965680949) — do not call /logout in tests. Auto-reply MUST be left DISABLED after test runs (autouse fixture handles this). Frontend has the Isabella-in-assign-modal bug — main agent should filter it out in WhatsAppChatLayout.js AssignModal (likely just adding a .filter(u => u.email !== 'isabella@ia.local') on attendants list before rendering picks).
rca of the issue: Isabella filter missing in frontend AssignModal: api.waBaileysAttendants() returns ALL users including Isabella (by design — backend includes her so the conv list can show 'Isabella (IA)' as the current assignee). The frontend modal should filter her out client-side because she's the AI placeholder, not a human attendant. Spec: 'list of attendants (Isabella IA filtered out)'. Fix: in WhatsAppChatLayout.js render of pick list: items.filter(u => u.email !== 'isabella@ia.local' && !u.is_ai_agent).
